questions.question: James Augustus Hickey is also known as father of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Journalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• James Augustus Hicky was an Irishman who launched the first printed newspaper in India, Hickey's Bengal Gazette.
 
• The Bombay Samachar, now Mumbai Samachar, is the oldest continuously published newspaper in India established in 1822 by Fardunjee Marzban, it is published in Gujarati and English. 
 
• The Lahore Chronicle was started by Syed Muhammad Azim, father of the Punjab historian, in 1849.

 
• Hickeys Bengal Gazette or the Original Calcutta General Advertiser was an English language weekly newspaper published in Kolkata (then Calcutta), the capital of British India.
 
• It was the first newspaper printed in Asia and was published for two years, between 1780 and 1782, before the East India Company seized the newspaper's types and printing press.
 
• Founded by James Augustus Hickey a highly eccentric Irishman who had previously spent two years in jail for debt, the newspaper was a strong critic of the administration of Governor-General Warren Hastings. 
 
• The newspaper was important for its provocative journalism and its fight for free expression in India.
 
• Hickey first maintained a neutral editing policy (his slogan was "Open to all Parties, but Influenced by None") but after he learned that competitors with ties to the East India Company were intending to launch a rival newspaper, the India Gazette, he changed his editorial stance.
 
• Hickey accused an East India Company employee, Simeon Droz, of supporting the India Gazette as punishment for Hickey's refusal to pay a bribe to Droz and Marian Hastings, Warren Hastings' wife.
 
• Hickey claimed Hastings' order violated his right to free expression and accused Hastings of corruption, tyranny.
 
• Hickey also accused other British leaders in Calcutta of corruption, including the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, Elijah Impey of taking bribes, and the leader of the Protestant Mission, Johann Zacharias Kiernander of stealing from an orphaned children's fund.
 
• Hickey's editorial independence was short-lived as Hastings and Kiernander sued him for libel. After four dramatic trials in June 1781, the Supreme Court found Hickey guilty and sentenced him to jail.
 
• Hickey continued to print his newspaper from jail and continued to accuse Hastings and others of corruption.

questions.question: When calculating Net National Product (NNP), what is deducted from Gross National Product (GNP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Depreciation**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP) **measures the total value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents within a specific time period, including income earned by residents from investments abroad.
 
• Depreciation accounts for the reduction in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear or obsolescence.
 
• By subtracting **depreciation from GNP, you arrive at Net National Product (NNP),** which reflects the actual value of goods and services produced, taking into account the loss of value in capital assets.
 
• The formula can be summarized as:** NNP=GNP−Depreciation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidies**

 
 
• Subsidies are government financial assistance provided to individuals or businesses to **promote economic activity **and** reduce costs**.
 
• They include direct cash payments, tax breaks, price supports, and grants.
 
• Subsidies can stimulate growth and lower consumer prices but may also cause market distortions and strain government budgets.
 
• Common examples include** agricultural subsidies, energy subsidies for renewables**, and education subsidies for higher education.
 
 
 
• **Indirect taxes**
 
 
• Indirect taxes are taxes levied on goods and services rather than on income or profits, meaning they are **not directly paid by the individual but are passed on through the price of goods.**
 
• Common forms of indirect taxes include sales tax,** value-added tax (VAT),** excise duty, and customs duty.
 
• Indirect taxes increase the cost of goods and services, which can lead to higher prices for consumers, making them less visible than direct taxes.
 
• Indirect taxes are a significant **source of revenue for governments**, as they are easier to collect and can be applied to a wide range of products and services.
 
 
 
• **Personal income**
 
 
• Personal income refers to the **total earnings received by an individual from various sources,** including wages, salaries, investments, rental income, and government benefits.
 
• It includes wages, bonuses, interest income, dividends, rents, and any other forms of **earnings before taxes are deducted.**
 
• Personal income is a **key indicator of an individual's economic** health and purchasing power, influencing consumption, savings, and overall economic activity.
 
• Personal income is subject to income tax, which varies based on the individual's income level and applicable tax laws in their country or region.

• This theory posits that iron technology was introduced to India through cultural diffusion from the Near **East or Central Asia,** likely via trade or migration.
